summary: Backend-only QA of the FIXED /api/tenant/utilities/scan + new /api/admin/tenant-utilities endpoints on Railway prod. 15 pytest cases executed against https://ross-house-backend-production.up.railway.app; 12 PASSED, 3 FAILED — all 3 failures share ONE root cause: the Emergent LLM key is NOT configured in Railway's env (EMERGENT_LLM_KEY missing). Every scan call returns HTTP 500 with `{"detail":"No hay API key configurada para AI Vision"}`. The emergentintegrations import itself works (no missing dependency error) — the issue is purely env config. Auth gates (401 without token, 403 for non-admin), 400 for missing body, full tenant CRUD + summary, admin tenant-utilities listing with pagination/filters, and the admin /utility-ocr/extract regression all pass cleanly. Admin OCR works which proves emergentintegrations is installed and EMERGENT_LLM_KEY *is* available somewhere in the admin path — but the tenant scan path can't see it (or admin OCR uses a different key var). NEEDS INVESTIGATION: either set EMERGENT_LLM_KEY on Railway service or fix the env var name lookup in tenant_utilities_router.py.

critical.issue: 500 'No hay API key configurada para AI Vision' on every call (invalid base64, oversized payload, AND valid JPEG). Root cause: `os.getenv('EMERGENT_LLM_KEY') or os.getenv('OPENAI_API_KEY','')` returns empty on Railway. The env var is not set on the production service (or its name differs). Meanwhile POST /api/admin/utility-ocr/extract on the same Railway instance returns 200 with extracted data — so emergentintegrations is installed AND a key is available in that code path. Likely fix: (a) set EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in Railway env, OR (b) align tenant_utilities_router.py to read whatever variable utility_ocr_router.py reads.

Validation ordering bug: the api-key check happens BEFORE base64 validation and size check. As a result, even sending invalid base64 or a >10 MB payload yields 500 (api key error) instead of 400/413. Fix: move the `if not llm_key` check inside the try-block AFTER `base64.b64decode` and the size guard. Also change status from 500 → 503 since 'no api key configured' is a service-availability issue, not a server bug.

rca_of_issue: FIX VERIFICATION RESULT: The CODE fix is correct (emergentintegrations import works, no missing-dependency error, no api.openai.com direct call). HOWEVER the fix is INVISIBLE in production because Railway is missing the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY env var for the tenant scan path. Evidence: (1) `from emergentintegrations.llm.chat import LlmChat` would raise 'AI Vision no disponible (emergentintegrations missing)' if the dep was unavailable — we get a different error message ('No hay API key configurada para AI Vision'), proving the import path succeeded. (2) /api/admin/utility-ocr/extract returns 200 with real LLM output on the same Railway instance, proving emergentintegrations + a key works for the admin code path. Therefore tenant_utilities_router.py:309 is reading the wrong env var, or the admin path reads a hard-coded value, or Railway has the key under a different name only available to the admin module. Reproduction: `curl -X POST $URL/api/tenant/utilities/scan -H 'Authorization: Bearer <tenant_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"image_base64":"<any base64>"}'` → 500. Mitigation: align env var name and/or set EMERGENT_LLM_KEY on Railway, then re-run the suite.
